title: Geo-Expansion Request Flow — Enterprise Intake to Operational Rollout
creator: Anjali Rao
description: Create a single, repeatable product + operational playbook to intake enterprise requests for new region availability and strict data residency constraints, prioritize them against existing roadmap and capacity, and produce an operational rollout plan that includes failover windows, SLAs, and compliance checkpoints.
background: Over the last 12 months we have received ad-hoc enterprise requests for new regions and strict residency (e.g., EU-only, APAC-residency). These are handled case-by-case. The lack of a consistent intake and prioritization flow increases lead time, causes capacity planning surprises for Dedicated, and risks missed compliance checks. This ticket consolidates learnings into an actionable intake->evaluate->prioritize->rollout playbook tailored to enterprise needs.
success_metrics: Median time from initial customer request to deployment plan <= 30 days
95% of region requests pass security & legal checklist within first two review iterations
Reduction in ad-hoc escalations to SRE during rollouts by 60%
Clear handoff artifacts for Sales/SEs: intake form + estimated TTM + compliance gating status
scope: Formalize intake form and triage rubric for region/residency requests
Define prioritization criteria (customer value, compliance risk, engineering effort, capacity impact)
Produce standardized rollout steps (canary, capacity pre-warm, DNS failover plan)
Integrate mandatory security/legal signoff checkpoints and KMS/HSM requirements into flow
Create templated customer-facing delivery commitments (SLA/ETA language)
out_of_scope: Provisioning of third-party cloud capacity (procurement remains with infra teams)
Custom per-customer network peering automation (handled by Dedicated professional services)
Changes to core serving runtime kernel selection (will be a follow-on ENG project if required)
stakeholders: Engineering: Priya Kaur (runtime lead), Samir Patel (SRE)
intake_flow_steps: 1) Intake form submission by SE/CS (link) with customer profile, residency requirement, expected QPS and SLA needs
2) PM Triage within 3 business days: assign priority tag and initial ETA estimate
3) Technical feasibility assessment by ENG (48–72h): capacity delta, network constraints, KV cache impacts
4) Compliance/legal review kickoff (3–5 business days) for data residency and KMS requirements
5) Cost & procurement note produced for Dedicated/reserved-capacity if required
6) Final decision: Approve -> Create rollout epic; Defer -> Communicate rationale and requeue; Decline -> Offer alternatives
prioritization_criteria: Customer strategic value (ARR, expansion likelihood) — weight: 35%
Regulatory urgency / legal mandate (e.g., contractual residency requirement) — weight: 30%
Operational risk (SLA impact, failover complexity) — weight: 10%
evaluation_checklist: Data residency footprint: which artifacts must not leave the target region (logs, embeddings, models)?
Network egress requirements and approved cloud regions
KMS/HSM integration and key residency constraints
Audit logging and retention policy changes
SLA and failover expectations (RPO/RTO), required DR windows
Billing model (hosted vs. dedicated) and anticipated unit-cost delta
Compatibility check with existing model variants and quantization profiles
Impact to autoscaling policies and burst capacity controls
rollout_playbook: Phase 0: Plan — define SLOs, capacity delta, security control list, and rollback criteria
Phase 1: Staging — deploy model variant into staging region, run perf & correctness evals using customer prompt set
Phase 2: Canary — limit traffic (5–10%) for 48–72 hours, monitor latency, error rates, cost per token
Phase 3: Gradual Ramp — increase to target capacity using pre-defined autoscale policy, validate KV cache hit ratios
Phase 4: Cutover & Failover Test — execute simulated failover, validate DNS and routing fallbacks, exercise KMS failover
Phase 5: Post-Mortem & Handover — publish runbook, update Console region catalog, schedule follow-up health checks
risks_mitigations: Risk: Unexpected latency increase due to KV cache cold-starts. Mitigation: pre-warm cache with representative prompt sets and enable prefix caching where applicable.
Risk: Regulatory review takes >2 cycles. Mitigation: parallelize legal + security reviews; provide a templated artifact package to speed approvals.
Risk: Capacity contention with existing customers. Mitigation: reserve burst lanes in Dedicated or offer staged rollout windows.
Risk: Cost overruns on hosted plan. Mitigation: provide clear cost delta estimate and optional dedicated pricing path.
Risk: SRE availability for cutover. Mitigation: schedule cutovers during SRE on-call overlap and create a one-button rollback path.
open_questions: Should we expose a self-serve region request form in Console for mid-market customers?
What is the minimum QPS threshold that should trigger Dedicated capacity discussions?
Do we need a formal legal template for cross-border data processing agreements (DPA addendum)?
Who owns the final customer ETA communication: PM or SE? Current preference: SE front-line with PM-provided ETA
